claims.text: AI legal research tools reduce hallucinations relative to general-purpose chatbots such as GPT-4.
AI legal research tools from LexisNexis and Thomson Reuters hallucinate between 17% and 33% of the time.
Proprietary AI legal research tools exhibit substantial differences in responsiveness across systems.
Proprietary AI legal research tools exhibit substantial differences in accuracy across systems.

evidence.description: While hallucinations are reduced relative to general-purpose chatbots (GPT-4)...
...we find that the AI research tools made by LexisNexis (Lexis+ AI) and Thomson Reuters (Westlaw AI-Assisted Research and Ask Practical Law AI) each hallucinate between 17% and 33% of the time.
We also document substantial differences between systems in responsiveness...

methodologies.name: Preregistered empirical evaluation of legal AI tools
methodologies.description: A preregistered empirical evaluation assessing the reliability, responsiveness, and accuracy of RAG-based proprietary legal AI research tools.

limitations.text: Large language models used in legal research tools are prone to hallucinate or make up false information.
Systematically assessing legal AI research tools is challenging due to the closed nature of proprietary systems.
